scope: Primary-source research and small analytical probes. No new observations, dark-matter detection, nonlinear AeST evolution or validation of a universe-collision model.

classifications.established_result: Mathematical result under stated assumptions, standard physical consequence, or experimental observation within its measured domain.
classifications.conditional_model: Derived or simulated result for specified equations, initial data, approximations and parameters.
classifications.untested_conjecture: A proposed physical explanation whose application here has not been established.
classifications.own_inference: A synthesis, counterexample, derivation or suggested discriminant produced in this pass. It is not an observation.

sources.authors: Emmy Noether; English translation by M. A. Tavel
sources.title: Invariant Variation Problems
sources.pointer: Section 1, formulation of the theorems; subsequent variational proof
sources.inspected: Primary translated PDF opening and theorem framing
sources.supports: Continuous action symmetries yield conservation identities under the theorem's hypotheses.
sources.limits: A conserved charge does not preserve each object. Global conserved energy requires the relevant spacetime structure and boundary conditions.

sources.authors: STAR Collaboration
sources.title: Measurement of e+e- Momentum and Angular Distributions from Linearly Polarized Photon Collisions
sources.pointer: Abstract and reported momentum and angular distributions in ultraperipheral Au+Au collisions
sources.inspected: Primary abstract and reported experimental summary
sources.supports: Observed electron-positron pairs and angular structure consistent with photon-photon production in the electromagnetic fields of relativistic nuclei.
sources.limits: Not a collision of universes and not production from nothing. The report's invariant threshold calculation is standard two-photon kinematics.

sources.authors: Hoernisa Iminniyaz, Manuel Drees, Xuelei Chen
sources.title: Relic Abundance of Asymmetric Dark Matter
sources.pointer: Section 2, equations 2 and 6-10; section 3 for the late abundance approximation
sources.inspected: Primary full-text HTML, assumptions and abundance equations
sources.supports: Pair-only annihilation conserves the difference of entropy-normalized yields while their sum evolves.
sources.limits: Assumes adiabatic cosmology and no later source, decay or same-species annihilation. The present probe begins after inverse production is negligible and does not reproduce a full thermal freeze-out calculation.

sources.authors: A. D. Sakharov
sources.title: Violation of CP invariance, C asymmetry, and baryon asymmetry of the universe
sources.pointer: JETP Letters 5, 24-27, original proposal; opening paragraph reproduced in the CERN lecture document
sources.inspected: Primary bibliographic record and reproduced opening of the original paper
sources.supports: Producing a baryon asymmetry is a separate problem from preserving an initial excess through annihilation.
sources.limits: Used for the historical proposal involving baryon-number violation and asymmetric processes, not as a newly established origin of the observed asymmetry.

sources.authors: C. Ryu, M. F. Andersen, P. Clade, Vasant Natarajan, K. Helmerson, W. D. Phillips
sources.title: Observation of persistent flow of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a toroidal trap
sources.pointer: Figures 2-5 and surrounding paragraphs about geometry, constriction, drift and vortex splitting
sources.inspected: Primary full-text HTML
sources.supports: Observed circulating flow survival changes with trap geometry and constriction; apparatus limits the ten-second observation.
sources.limits: Does not establish an infinite lifetime. Density zeros and changes in accessible configurations can allow winding to change.

sources.authors: T. W. B. Kibble
sources.title: Topology of cosmic domains and strings
sources.pointer: Sections 3-5: formation, topology and later evolution of defects
sources.inspected: Primary PDF abstract and introduction describing section scope
sources.supports: Allowed defect types depend on vacuum-manifold topology; formation and later evolution are distinct questions.
sources.limits: The existence of particular cosmic defects is not established by their mathematical possibility or by laboratory analogues.

sources.authors: Nir Navon, Alexander L. Gaunt, Robert P. Smith, Zoran Hadzibabic
sources.title: Critical Dynamics of Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking in a Homogeneous Bose gas
sources.pointer: Coherence-length dependence on quench rate; equations 1-2 and figure 4 as examined by the scales route
sources.inspected: Primary abstract and scales-route handoff
sources.supports: Experiment tests the dependence of coherence length on the rate of crossing a transition.
sources.limits: Does not identify a galactic universality class. Later coarsening is a proposed separate survival probe, not a new measurement here.

sources.authors: Asimina Arvanitaki, Masha Baryakhtar, Xinlu Huang
sources.title: Discovering the QCD Axion with Black Holes and Gravitational Waves
sources.pointer: Section III B, equations 23-25; equation 8 for occupation and section II for superradiance
sources.inspected: Primary PDF downloaded and relevant text read
sources.supports: A real-boson cloud's occupation can grow by superradiance and decline by pair annihilation while retaining a recognizable spatial mode.
sources.limits: Rates and astronomical abundance depend on particle and black-hole properties. Historical event forecasts and exclusions were not treated as current observational results.

sources.authors: S. Erne, R. Buecker, T. Gasenzer, J. Berges, J. Schmiedmayer
sources.title: Observation of universal dynamics in an isolated one-dimensional Bose gas far from equilibrium
sources.pointer: Equation 1; figures 2-4; text accompanying figure 4 on particle and energy transport
sources.inspected: Primary PDF downloaded and relevant experimental discussion read
sources.supports: Measured evolving low-momentum scaling, approximate number conservation in the moving scaling region, and energy redistribution outside it after preparation.
sources.limits: The cooling quench first removes energetic atoms. Subsequent redistribution does not show that every isolated system condenses or that gravity shares this exponent.

sources.authors: Edward Seidel, Wai-Mo Suen
sources.title: Formation of Solitonic Stars Through Gravitational Cooling
sources.pointer: Sections I-II and figures 1-3; downloaded TeX lines 115-153, 210-244 and 264-306
sources.inspected: Original 1993 arXiv TeX retrieved and read after PDF retrieval failed
sources.supports: Self-gravitating massive scalar configurations can form bound objects by ejecting scalar-field energy without electromagnetic cooling.
sources.limits: Spherical examples demonstrate existence, not a universal efficiency. These are Einstein-Klein-Gordon and related Newtonian models, not AeST. Historical dark-matter exclusions are not adopted.

sources.authors: Cora Uhlemann, Michael Kopp, Thomas Haugg
sources.title: Schrodinger method as N-body double and UV completion of dust
sources.pointer: Sections II.2 and II.4; equations 13-14; section IV.2 and figures 3-7
sources.inspected: Primary full-text HTML, Madelung equations and numerical collapse example
sources.supports: A single wavefunction and its smoothed phase-space distribution can describe momentum dispersion and multistream behavior through shell crossing.
sources.limits: Its pointwise Madelung velocity remains single valued away from nodes. Coarse phase-space streams are a distinct description. This is no derivation of AeST dynamics.

sources.authors: D. G. Levkov, A. G. Panin, I. I. Tkachev
sources.title: Gravitational Bose-Einstein condensation in the kinetic regime
sources.pointer: Equations 1-4; section 5 paragraph after equation 5; section 6 virial estimate
sources.inspected: Primary full-text HTML, kinetic assumptions, relaxation time and regime caveat
sources.supports: Gravitational condensation can occur with a calculable kinetic relaxation time in highly occupied boson systems.
sources.limits: Requires Rmv/hbar and mv^2 tau/hbar much greater than one. The section 6 coefficient assumes an approximate virial relation. Section 5 does not identify ordinary power-law turbulent cascades in its gravitational relaxation.

sources.authors: D. V. Semikoz, I. I. Tkachev
sources.title: Condensation of bosons in kinetic regime
sources.pointer: Abstract, weak lambda phi^4 interaction and two kinetic stages
sources.inspected: Primary abstract and publication record
sources.supports: Short-range scalar self-interactions support kinetic condensation with self-similar stages in the studied model.
sources.limits: This interaction kernel differs from gravitational Landau kinetics. No quantitative cascade result was transferred to AeST.

sources.authors: A. S. Dmitriev, D. G. Levkov, A. G. Panin, I. I. Tkachev
sources.title: Self-similar kinetics for gravitational Bose-Einstein condensation
sources.pointer: Equations 1-3; section IV equations 22-26; section V.2 equations 32-33
sources.inspected: Primary preprint HTML, overview and stationary-cascade analysis
sources.supports: Evolving gravitational kinetic profiles can be self-similar while a stationary power-law cascade has fluxes unsuitable for the condensation process studied.
sources.limits: Restricted kinetic approximation and source/boundary assumptions. The parameter D labels scaling, not a spatial fractal dimension. No general equivalence to short-range turbulence is asserted.

sources.authors: Marianthi Bataki, Constantinos Skordis, Tom Zlosnik
sources.title: Aether scalar tensor theory: Hamiltonian Formalism
sources.pointer: Section II equations 1-4; sections VI-VII and nonlinear degree-of-freedom count
sources.inspected: Primary HTML action, fields and conclusions
sources.supports: AeST includes scalar, vector and metric dynamics with six physical degrees of freedom. The stated action is the basis for the direct shift-current derivation.
sources.limits: A degree-of-freedom count is not a nonlinear collapse or energy-retention result. Stability on Minkowski backgrounds does not establish stability on every relevant background.

sources.authors: Constantinos Skordis, Tom Zlosnik
sources.title: New Relativistic Theory for Modified Newtonian Dynamics
sources.pointer: Equation 5 action; Cosmological observables paragraph deriving K_Q=I0/a^3; equations 9-12 and explicit non-closure paragraph
sources.inspected: Primary full-text HTML, action and perturbation-fluid discussion
sources.supports: Shift charge fixes a homogeneous dilution law with an initial-condition normalization. Effective pressure also depends on vector perturbations.
sources.limits: The cosmological linear system is not a closed ordinary dark fluid. It does not derive the notebook's nonlinear thermal floor.

sources.authors: Gavin E. Crooks
sources.title: Entropy production fluctuation theorem and the nonequilibrium work relation for free energy differences
sources.pointer: Equations 2, 5-7; section III preparation and reverse-process conditions
sources.inspected: Primary PDF text, microscopic reversibility and path probability derivation
sources.supports: A relation between forward and appropriately reversed path probabilities for specified stochastic dynamics and thermodynamic protocols.
sources.limits: Not a universal prescription for reversing the cosmos, and not an explanation for the cosmological low-entropy boundary condition.

sources.authors: Latham Boyle, Kieran Finn, Neil Turok
sources.title: CPT-Symmetric Universe
sources.pointer: Abstract; Introduction; Spacetime background and perturbations
sources.inspected: Primary HTML opening, continuation hypothesis and dark-matter symmetry
sources.supports: An example of a mathematically specified cosmological symmetry hypothesis with a proposed stable relic.
sources.limits: The state-level CPT assumption is additional to microscopic CPT symmetry. This is not a collision model or a consequence of reversing electron-positron annihilation. Its predictions were not adjudicated against current data here.

sources.authors: James R. A. Davenport and colleagues
sources.title: The Rise and Fall of the Eclipsing Binary HS Hydrae
sources.pointer: Abstract: combined DASCH and TESS history and cessation of eclipses
sources.inspected: Primary abstract, after evidence-route handoff
sources.supports: Observed eclipse disappearance can accompany survival of the underlying binary and changed orbital inclination.
sources.limits: Detailed instrumental selection and historical-data analysis belong to the evidence route. The predicted future return of eclipses was not used as an observed fact.

sources.authors: E. K. Anderson and the ALPHA Collaboration
sources.title: Observation of the effect of gravity on the motion of antimatter
sources.pointer: Abstract and likelihood analysis of the local gravitational acceleration
sources.inspected: Primary paper abstract and measurement summary
sources.supports: Antihydrogen released in the ALPHA-g apparatus is attracted toward Earth.
sources.limits: The reported acceleration has substantial uncertainty. This measurement does not establish arbitrary antimatter properties or any cosmological branch hypothesis.

own_work.claim: Exact post-production annihilation solution illustrates finite exposure and conserved excess as distinct survival mechanisms.
own_work.checks: RK4 agreement, conserved difference, symmetric limit
own_work.limits: No full freeze-out integration or astronomical abundance fit.

own_work.claim: A free standing wave has zero current and nonzero momentum variance and energy.
own_work.checks: Numerical normalization and first two momentum moments using exact derivatives
own_work.limits: Spatially averaged Wigner momentum streams do not make the pointwise Madelung velocity multivalued. Not a self-gravitating collapse calculation.

own_work.claim: An assumed scaling spectrum can conserve particle number in a moving band while its kinetic energy decreases.
own_work.checks: Simpson integration agrees with number and energy scaling exponents
own_work.limits: Profile and exponents are inputs. No kinetic equation or global energy reservoir is simulated.

own_work.claim: Direct variation of the AeST scalar terms gives a conserved shift current, with local boundary transport and homogeneous a^3 K_Q conservation.
own_work.checks: Analytic variation and agreement with the homogeneous relation stated in P16
own_work.limits: Not an energy-flux calculation, entropy law or proof of nonlinear stability. Higher-derivative extensions require a revised current.

own_work.claim: Observed populations should be separated into formation, survival and visibility factors when comparing relic explanations.
own_work.checks: Constructive mechanism comparison and the observed HS Hydrae example
own_work.limits: A general inference framework, not a fitted population model or new empirical discovery.
